name: cleanup_inventory
description:
Say what is on this machine that agents may have left: what is yours, what sessions that ended left,
caches, discoveries — new things no known kind covers — and how full the disk is. Changes nothing.

name: cleanup_plan
description:
Decide a cleanup and show it before anything is done: what will be removed and why, what is only
reported because nothing proves it is an agent's, what is kept. Pass the planId to cleanup_apply
within 10 minutes; after that the plan is stale.

scope.description: mine (this session's), orphans (left by ended sessions), caches (shared caches that rebuild themselves) or everything; mine by default.

name: cleanup_apply
description: Carry out the removals of a plan cleanup_plan showed, in its order. Each thing is checked again first and left alone if it changed.

only.description: Ids of the plan's removals to carry out; all of them when omitted.

name: cleanup_release
description: Release one thing now, such as a simulator or an emulator you acquired, if it is proven yours or an ended session's.

id.description: Its id as cleanup_inventory printed it, such as simulator:<udid>.

name: cleanup_keep
description: Ask for something to be left alone by every cleanup, with the reason, or withdraw that.

id.description: Its id as cleanup_inventory printed it.

reason.description: Why it stays; required unless withdrawing.

withdraw.description: True to let cleanups have it again.

name: cleanup_learn
description:
Turn a discovery into a known kind: a rule written to rules.json covering every trace like it from now
on. ignore says it is harmless, report shows it as a leftover, cache makes it a shared cache.

pattern.description: Keys it covers: * is one path segment, ** any number, ~ is home; such as ~/Library/Caches/tool/*.

trail.description: The trail of the discovery, the part of its id before the colon; file by default.

note.description: Why the rule exists, for the person who reads rules.json.

blockedWhileRunning.description: A program that keeps what it covers open, such as Code; nothing covered is removed while it runs.

name: cleanup_simulator_acquire
description:
Get an iOS simulator of your own: a clone of a shut-down device, or a new device of a type, named for
this session so that no other agent uses it and only this session's cleanup removes it. Use it instead
of booting a simulator somebody may already be using, and drive it by the udid it returns.

from.description: A shut-down device to clone, by name or udid, or a device type such as iPhone 17 Pro; the newest iPhone Pro when omitted.

boot.description: Whether to boot it and wait until it is ready; false by default.

name: cleanup_emulator_acquire
description:
Get an Android emulator of your own: a new virtual device from an installed system image, started on a
free console port without saving a snapshot, named for this session so that only its cleanup removes
it. It returns the adb serial at once; the device needs a minute or two to boot.

image.description: Part of an installed system image path, such as android-37.0 or google_apis; the newest image without the Play Store when omitted.

window.description: Whether to show the emulator's window; false runs it headless.

name: cleanup_run
description:
Start a program that keeps running — a dev server, a watcher, a worker — written down as yours from its
first second, so that cleaning up after this session ends it for certain and nothing of anyone else's.
It returns at once with the process id and a log file; read the log for its output. Prefer it to
starting such a program in the background from a shell.

command.description: The whole command line, run by zsh, such as npm run dev -- --port 3000.

directory.description: Directory to run it in; the server's own working directory when omitted.

name: find_tool
description: Find which of this server's tools does a thing, described in your own words, with every argument each one takes.

task.description: What you want to do, such as «free the port my dev server held».

limit.description: How many tools to return at most; 5 by default.

name: cleanup_diagnose
description:
Say what state this server is in: its version, the session it counts as yours, and which of the
programs it works through (simctl, adb, docker) it can reach. Call it when another tool reports that
something is unavailable, not before every task.
